All this David handed over to Solomon, so that he would do everything in the house of the Lord according to the pattern that God had made known to David, for the house of God is too great to be arranged by a man, but God Himself arranges His house and man carries out what God declares, as He declared of old to Moses the details of the tabernacle of meeting (Ex 25:8, 9).

entries.section: (2) David's charge to Solomon and his handing over to him the plan for building the house

paragraphs.text: In the end David encouraged Solomon to do all that God had charged, and David's strong relationship with God appears in his saying "God, even my God," to call his son to this intimate relationship. He promised him that God would be with him until he completed the building of His house, and encouraged him not to fear any obstacles, or problems, or enemies that might appear before him, especially since Solomon had not yet completed twenty years of age at that time. God fulfilled His promise, so Solomon was strengthened and was not troubled by those who rebelled against him, and he completed the house of the Lord with all diligence.

entries.section: (2) David's charge to Solomon and his handing over to him the plan for building the house

paragraphs.text: Skilful with wisdom: one who has a craft, an artist and gifted in it.

David reminded Solomon that he had arranged for him the divisions of the priests and the Levites and the chiefs and the artists who were able to do the work of the house of the Lord and everything in it, and all the people, all of whom would help him to complete this great work. Donations for the Temple, and David's prayer and death

David continued his words with the leaders of his people, whom he had gathered in (ch. 28:1), and showed them that because of the young age of Solomon, whom God alone chose from among all his brothers to be king after him over His people, and likewise God's command that Solomon would be the one to build the Temple of God, and that the Temple is for God and not for man, that is, it is very great and no man is able to build it except with God's help, he had therefore prepared all that he could prepare for this Temple, as will appear in (v. 2).
Onyx stones: a precious stone in which colors appear in parallel lines.
Setting: adorning.
Kohl-black stones: very black, or white with parts that are very black.
Spotted: white with black spots.

Here David mentioned the kinds of materials that he had prepared for the building of the Temple of the Lord, which contain everything that is precious, whether gold, or silver, or precious stones, and this shows how great was David's love and magnification of God, and that he prepared with all his energy all that he was able, for he says "with all my might," and whoever gives to God with all his energy receives a blessing beyond what he imagines.
Ophir: a region in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, distinguished by mines of pure gold, and it is present-day Yemen.
Talent: it has several weights ranging between 20 and 40 kg.

In addition to what David had prepared for the house of the Lord from the treasuries of the kingdom, he also offered from his own money huge quantities of pure gold and refined silver and gave them to those in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord, whom he assigned for this work. This gold was for overlaying the walls of the house of the Lord on the inside. And this shows two things:
1- David's heartfelt love for God, so he gives of his own money, because he has nothing dearer than God.
2- David's generosity in giving, so he gives abundantly the best he has to God.

Giving to God shows how much you love Him, for it is your opportunity to express your love and your non-attachment to material things, that is, your esteem of God above everything in the world. And know that giving to any person in need, or to the Church, is very precious in the sight of God, indeed it is your way to enter the Kingdom.
Offers willingly: donates.
To consecrate his service (to fill his hand) to the Lord: gives to God generously.
Rulers of the work: those in charge, or the heads of the various crafts, who take part in the building of the house of God.

After David showed his concern to give to the house of God, to be an example to the leaders and the people, when he gave what he had prepared to the heads of the various crafts, and David of course did not intend to boast or be proud, but wanted to encourage everyone to give, he asked the leaders of the people, who among you wishes to donate abundantly to the house of God? David did not wish to bind the people and the leaders to fixed sums, but wanted the donation to result from their love of God, that is, to be completely voluntary.
A dram of gold: about 8 grams.

The leaders of the people were eager and gave generously to the house of the Lord gold, silver, brass, iron and precious stones, and they gave them to Jehiel, who was in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

When David and the people gave to the house of the Lord, God favored them with joy, since they were counted worthy to share in the building of the house of God, that He might dwell in their midst. And this is a grace that God pours out on everyone who gives to God with all his heart.

After David had remained for a period lying on his bed because of his old age, he now strengthened himself and stood before the congregation, to bless them not while he was in his bed but in their presence, and he prayed his prayer, which was a model for his people, and indeed for all of us until now in speaking with God, as he begins it by blessing the Lord God of Israel. Here the humility of God appears, that He is named after His people, so He is called the God of Israel, and David declares that God is blessed in Himself from eternity and to eternity, so He has no need of the praise of men, and this shows David's faith and humility.

David continues his praise, and declares that to God belong greatness, power, glory and all that is connected with them, for He is the Creator of the universe, that is, heaven and earth, and He is also above all the gods that men think to be gods, because the works of God surpass all that men ascribe to the pagan gods.
Of thee: from You.

David completes his praise, saying that to God belong riches and honor, indeed dominion over all men and creation, and consequently God alone is able to strengthen men and support them. Because of all these attributes of God, David says that He is worthy of praise. And praise is the greatest of prayers, because it is pure love for God, without any request of Him.

With great humility David declares his weakness, and that of all his people, and his unworthiness to offer anything to God, namely the gifts offered for the building of His Temple, because God is the Creator of everything, so what man offers to God is His own, as if man takes from the hand of God and then gives it back into His hand, so giving is a grace from God to man, so that he may feel that he is offering something to God, because the Owner of everything in the world is God alone.

David shows his love for God in his description of himself and of all who believe in God as strangers and sojourners in this world, and consequently not attached to material things, so that they give them easily and with joy to God, since their only aim is the eternal Kingdom. David feels that all the fathers from the days of Abraham lived as strangers, so he is a stranger like them, even if he is a king and has much gold and possessions and greatness, because the love of God has taken possession of his heart and covered over everything, and all that he prepared and offered for the Temple of God is originally God's own.

David shows his faith in God, for He is the searcher of hearts and reins and rejoices in the love of His children for Him, and therefore David and his people came forward to give gifts to the house of God, that they might rejoice in this blessing, to offer to God and for God to rejoice in them. Here David's heartfelt love for God appears, for he offers his heart before his material gifts.

David intercedes through the fathers whom God blessed before, and entreats His mercies, that the feelings of love for God may remain in the hearts of His people, and that God may establish them in them and prepare their hearts every day to be attached to His love, and this by keeping His commandments. And God's dwelling in the hearts of His people is more important than His dwelling in a house made with hands.

Here David makes a special petition for his son Solomon, that his whole heart may be for God, so that he may be concerned for the building of the house of God, whose materials David had prepared, and keep the commandments of God and live by them. And this shows the importance of the leader, for if he is spiritual he will lead his people in life with God.

Be concerned for your spiritual life, because you are an example to those around you and you influence them without speaking, so keep the commandments of God and be concerned for His service with all your heart, even if you do not see the completion of what you are doing, or receive any praise, as David prepared the materials for building the Temple though he knew that he would not build it.

David appears as a great spiritual leader in calling his people to bless God as he did, so they obeyed him and blessed the Lord and bowed down before Him and before the king, and this was a declaration from them of their support for every word David had said in his prayer, that is, David was the tongue that spoke for the hearts of all his people.

entries.section: (3) The offering of sacrifices and the enthroning of Solomon

paragraphs.text: On the day after David's prayer and his giving of blessing to God, and the people after him, the people gathered and offered peace offerings to God in abundance, rejoicing at Solomon's being made king. The numbers of these sacrifices were a thousand bullocks, and likewise rams, and also lambs. And they ate of the sacrifices before God and made Solomon king the second time, and with him was Zadok the high priest, who remained with him, because Abiathar, the other high priest, had taken part in the conspiracy of Adonijah, and so was removed, that is, Zadok became the only high priest for all the people, and therefore it says "and Zadok to be priest," and this was mentioned in (1 Kgs 2:35). The first enthroning of Solomon was when Zadok the high priest poured the oil on Solomon's head and he entered Jerusalem with a great procession (1 Kgs 1:39, 40). Solomon here is like David, who was anointed by the hand of Samuel while he was in his father's house, but reigned many years later, after Saul died.

David and Solomon are types of Christ, who first reigned over the hearts of those who believe in Him by His Incarnation and His redemption of them and the descent of His Holy Spirit upon them, and will then reign completely a second time on the last day, at His Second Coming, when He casts Satan into eternal torment and glorifies those who believe in Him with Him in the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) The offering of sacrifices and the enthroning of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Thus Solomon was proclaimed king over the people of God in the lifetime of David, and all the chiefs and mighty men submitted to him, since God gave him grace and awe in their eyes, despite his young age. All his brothers also submitted to him. And the divine majesty that God gave to Solomon surpassed any majesty given to another king over Israel.

God is ready to give you awe in the eyes of those around you, however great your weakness, if you trust in Him and are humble, and He will work through you with all power, for the glory of His holy name.

This event was mentioned in (1 Kgs 2:11, 12). After David made his son Solomon king, having completed forty years on the throne, seven of them over the tribe of Judah in Hebron and thirty-three years over all Israel in Jerusalem, when his age at that time was seventy years (2 Sam 5:4, 5), David died in a good old age, because his life was good and pleased God, so that God ascribed the kings who came from his descendants to him, and even Christ Himself was ascribed to David, in magnification of David's righteousness and his love for God.
God regards every good work you do very highly, and in the end, when you leave this world, you will have a great place in heaven, according to your goodness.

What was written here about David, and also what was written in the books of Samuel and the beginning of the First Book of Kings, was recorded, in addition to other accounts, in special historical books that are not among the books of the Bible, namely the acts of Samuel the prophet, the acts of Nathan the prophet and the acts of Gad the seer.
